clue.text: Be crazy and feel obliged to go up on the roof?

definitions.meaning: to be slightly mad or not quite all there, in an informal idiom

definitions.text: feel obliged to go up on the roof?
definitions.meaning: read literally, someone whose roof tile has come adrift ought to climb up and fix it

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for mild madness is taken literally: a roof with a tile adrift needs someone to climb up to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being a little unhinged, like having a screw loose.

clue.text: Worker catching bus, dishevelled spouse

indicators.note: the worker word holds the other letters as if it had caught them

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker or labourer

indicators.note: untidy or messed up, so the letters of bus are jumbled

explanation.surface: A labourer grabbing a crowded bus arrives looking scruffy, and turns out to be someone's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' is the old sense of a hired hand, and the surface's crowded bus is the anagram fodder rather than transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A married man is his wife's spouse.

clue.text: Page — one used to bowing?

definitions.meaning: the heroine of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night disguises herself as a page boy
a stringed instrument is played with a bow, rather than someone bowing their head

explanation.walkthrough: Bowing here is drawing a bow across strings, not bending at the waist as a page might.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both Shakespeare's disguised servant girl and an instrument played with a bow.

clue.text: Biblical tribesman observed a cock bird of prey

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a kite is a hawk-like raptor

explanation.surface: A man of an Old Testament tribe watches a rooster and a hawk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament people descended from Amalek were enemies of the Israelites.

clue.text: Left what's beginning to roast in oven

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what's that?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word roast is wanted here

explanation.surface: Someone has left whatever is starting to cook in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's' is the query 'eh?', a short way of asking 'what's that?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A glassmaker's annealing furnace is a kind of kiln or oven.

clue.text: Sailor with minimal clothing on leaves

parts.note: tar is an old word for a seaman
a rag is a scrap of clothing

explanation.surface: A sailor wearing next to nothing lies on a bed of leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb is the plant's aromatic foliage, used in cooking.

clue.text: Philosopher almost went rigid

indicators.note: nearly the whole word, so its final letter is lopped off

parts.note: locked means seized up or became fixed

explanation.surface: A thinker very nearly froze stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of LOCKED.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke was a seventeenth-century English empiricist thinker.

clue.text: Speak up and get the better of encounter

parts.note: to outwit is to outsmart someone
to hit is to come upon or meet, as in hit a snag

explanation.surface: Say what you mean and beat the opponent you meet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an urging to tell what you know, to speak plainly.

clue.text: Pledge demanding serious attention

definitions.meaning: a sum paid as a token of good faith, a deposit

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a down payment or token, and the adjective means grave and sincere.

clue.text: Decorative panel shows bear pursued by monarch

parts.note: to stomach is to tolerate or bear
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An ornamental panel depicts a bear being chased by a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an ornamental triangular piece worn on the front of a bodice in Tudor dress.

clue.text: Provide food going cold, consumed with relish at first

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ate means consumed

indicators.note: the initial letter alone of the word relish is used

explanation.surface: Food served cold is eaten with pickle as a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay on meals for guests is to supply catering.

clue.text: A complex network has daughter dumbfounded

parts.note: a maze is a confusing network of paths
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A tangled network leaves a daughter bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean astonished, utterly surprised.

clue.text: Has she reached a limit?

parts.note: to make a place is to reach it, as in made it home
a line is a boundary or limit

explanation.surface: A question of whether a woman has hit her ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'she' is the definition: this is a girl's name, built from 'made' and 'line'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Territory to visit as tourist, by the sea

parts.note: to do a city is to tour it
the main is a poetic term for the open ocean

explanation.surface: A region worth sightseeing on the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a realm or area ruled or controlled.

clue.text: Is potentially reaching a peak in traditional craft

parts.note: may expresses possibility, as in it may be
to flower is to reach full bloom or prime

explanation.surface: Folk handicraft could be at its height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' means a vessel, not a handicraft: the ship that carried the Pilgrim Fathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pilgrim Fathers' ship is a famous vessel, the craft of tradition.

clue.text: What has little possibility of happening — a hole in one?

definitions.text: What has little possibility of happening
definitions.meaning: an outside chance, an unlikely event
a golf ace from the tee is a far-reaching stroke

explanation.definitionFit: It is both an improbable chance and, playfully, a distant stroke in golf.

clue.text: Victorian GEM happy to put on weight

parts.note: glad means happy
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A Victorian worthy is pleased to gain a few pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: GOM, Grand Old Man, was the nickname of the Victorian prime minister William Gladstone.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone, four times prime minister, was nicknamed the Grand Old Man.

clue.text: May the' heretic be for ever at rest near a river

parts.note: RIP, requiescat in pace, wishes the dead eternal rest
an Arian followed Arius, whose teaching was condemned as heresy

explanation.surface: A tombstone wish that a dissenter might lie in peace beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Arius denied Christ's full divinity, so his followers were branded heretics.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes banks of a stream, things on or beside a watercourse.

clue.text: Poet's idle ways misconstrued

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads poet is

indicators.note: misread or taken wrongly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A versifier's lazy habits are misunderstood.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Day-Lewis was an Anglo-Irish Poet Laureate.

clue.text: I'd burst out, creating trouble

indicators.note: the letters break out of their order and land in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they exploded and caused a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To bother or upset someone is to disturb them.

clue.text: Friend about to improve on computer

indicators.note: turned around, so the friend word is written backwards

parts.note: pal means friend
to top something is to better it

explanation.surface: A friend is about to upgrade a PC.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable personal computer is called a laptop.

clue.text: Colourful substance US investigators found in mine

indicators.note: the investigators are placed inside the mine word

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
G-men are FBI agents

explanation.surface: FBI agents uncover a dye in a mine shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a material that gives colour.

clue.text: Plant offering formula for the sick physician to get better?

definitions.meaning: a low-growing herb of the mint family used in folk medicine

definitions.text: offering formula for the sick physician to get better?
definitions.meaning: echoing the proverb physician, cure thyself

explanation.walkthrough: The second half recalls the Bible's 'Physician, heal thyself' (Luke 4:23).
explanation.definitionFit: It is a herb once used for wounds, and literally a doctor treating himself.

clue.text: Monster lurking in filthy drains

indicators.note: the answer hides within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A beast hides in dirty sewers.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the many-headed serpent slain by Hercules.

clue.text: Demanding, like the man in charge

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a king is a ruler in charge

explanation.surface: Being bossy, just like a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Requesting something is requiring or demanding it.

clue.text: Get used to conditions in river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Acclimatise to life in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To harden or accustom someone to hardship is to make them used to it.

clue.text: Finally, expelled weaselly individual in old school

indicators.note: the final letter is thrown out of the animal word

parts.note: a stoat is an animal of the weasel family

explanation.surface: A sly character is kicked out of a traditional school at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally, expelled' drops the last letter of STOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stoics took their name from the painted porch in Athens where Zeno taught.

clue.text: Keeping clear of any match

parts.note: a match is a marriage, so someone who avoids one remains single

explanation.definitionFit: Someone not married has stayed out of any wedding match.

clue.text: Bring in special reduction… 28… where counter profit is by low-value pieces, trash primarily

indicators.note: out of the ordinary, so the letters take an unusual order

explanation.surface: Launch a special price cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 28, whose clue completes the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To present or bring forward something new is to introduce it.

clue.text: … where counter profit is by low-value pieces, trash primarily

parts.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served
gain means profit
base means of low worth, as in base metal
men are pieces in chess or draughts

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word trash is taken

explanation.surface: A discount store where bar takings come from cheap goods and junk.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with 27: 'special reduction ... where' defines the store floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The basement floor of a store selling goods cheaply is where reductions are.
